The 5 Best Smart Rings, Tested by Fitness Editors

📅 31 Jan 2023 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved.
  • SMART RINGS HAVE swiftly become one of the most popular forms of health tracking on the market today.
  • One thing to be clear on: Smart rings and fitness trackers are not created equal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

SMART RINGS HAVE swiftly become one of the most popular forms of health tracking on the market today. These minimalist wearables deliver advanced health and fitness metrics—like sleep, recovery, readiness, and even stress tracking—without the bulk of a watch or the distraction of a screen. We put the most popular models through weeks of testing and spoke with experts to find the best smart rings for every kind of user.

One thing to be clear on: Smart rings and fitness trackers are not created equal. Smart rings definitely focus more on overall wellness while fitness trackers are more for dialing in on workout metrics. While smart rings still offer workout modes and step tracking, the workout metrics are not nearly as in-depth as those you’ll find on an Apple Watch or Garmin. But these devices offer a way to monitor your daily health-related metrics in a more subtle and discreet way. Whether you’re looking to track your sleep more accurately, understand your recovery needs, or monitor other daily health-related metrics, there’s a smart ring for you on this list.

In a recent development, as the Fitness and Reviews editor at Men’s Health, it’s my job to test the latest and greatest fitness tech, including smart rings. I’ve been a smart ring wearer since the first Oura Ring was released, and they’ve been an important tool in providing me with health data throughout the years.

In order to build this guide of the best smart rings, I gathered the most popular model of each brand on the market and tried them out for at least two weeks. I wore them during workouts, walks, writing, sleep, and ordinary errands around the home and out and about. This guide is the result of our experience and testing, and will be updated as new products are released.

Here is our guide to the best smart rings.

The Oura Ring continues to come out on top for us, even as we continue to test new more rings over the years. As the most up-to-date version of Oura’s popular smart ring, the Oura Ring 5 brings new sensors and algorithmic improvements to an already powerful health-tracking device. This version nixed the tangible sensors and cut back on the thickness to build an even sleeker, thinner, and more comfortable model—but don’t worry, the data has only improved with each iteration.

According to recent reports, from a health-tracking standpoint, the Oura Ring 5 gives you a holistic picture of your wellness: temperature variation, sleep analysis, blood oxygen monitoring, heart rate variability (HRV), resting heart rate, activity tracking, and daytime stress detection. If you wear it overnight, it automatically logs how long and how well you slept, how much time you spent in deep sleep, REM, and light sleep, and even gives you a readiness score each morning.

Recent findings suggest that I personally love the sleep-tracking feature on my Oura Ring. It’s definitely my most-utilized function—it’s the first thing I check every morning when I wake up. And I have to say, it’s highly accurate. I wake up at least once a night, and I’ll typically look at the clock when I do. When I check my Oura sleep metrics in the morning, it shows my midnight wake-up time almost exactly every time.

Read More: Our Hands-On Review of the Oura Ring 5.

Sources indicate that for those who want insights into sleep, heart rate, and recovery—without dropping $400 or signing up for a monthly membership—the RingConn Gen 2 Air offers great value. RingConn has refined its hardware with this second generation, offering a noticeably lighter and more comfortable fit than the original.

What makes RingConn different is its inclusion of sleep apnea detection, a rare find in this industry, especially without requiring a subscription. However, the Air does not offer this feature that RingConn is known for. The RingConn Gen 2 Air monitors a wide range of sleep metrics, including time spent in each sleep stage, movement during the night, and breathing irregularities. It’s an ideal ring for anyone trying to better understand how their overnight recovery impacts daily energy and long-term health, but it does not monitor sleep apnea like its sister product, the RingConn Gen 2.

I do have some qualms with the workout tracking. While those looking for in-depth fitness tracking are more likely to go with something like a Garmin or Whoop, the RingConn Gen 2 Air is especially basic when it comes to distinguishing different workouts. I wouldn’t really trust it to correctly judge what kind of workout I’m doing, but perhaps running. It can log activity and heart rate zones, but its technology for exercise auto-detection is latest this year and not entirely accurate yet.

In a recent development, still, for people more concerned with sleep and recovery than fitness performance, the Gen 2 Air is more than capable. Just note that sizes run slightly large, so it’s worth using their sizing kit or sizing down if you’re between sizes. The tech giant also released an updated version, the Gen 3 Air, but honestly, it’s more expensive, heavier, and still can’t compete with the Oura Ring. So better to stick with this version in my opinion.

Read More: Best Fitness Trackers.

Industry observers note that samsung’s long-awaited Galaxy Ring is a newer addition to the smart ring catalog. Crafted from lightweight titanium and available in three finishes, if you already use a Samsung Galaxy phone or smartwatch the integration takes no effort.

Industry observers note that designed to work seamlessly with Samsung Health, the Galaxy Ring tracks heart rate, activity, and sleep highly accurately. Its biggest selling point may be its emphasis on stress and sleep metrics, which have become central to Samsung’s wellness strategy. Galaxy Ring will even give you a sleep animal that reflects your sleep habits—dog is the golden ticket there. If you get, say, a turtle (you fall asleep slowly and may have some interruptions throughout the night), Galaxy AI will bring you a proposed plan of action to get your sleep back on track, taking sleep tracking to that next level. It also includes skin temperature sensors and supports auto workout detection for some activities, like walking and running.

While it lacks compatibility with iPhones, it does everything Android users need it to. And although Samsung hasn’t introduced a subscription plan yet, there’s speculation that one may arrive in the future to access advanced features. For now, all features are free, making it one of the most robust and cost-effective options for Android users. And if you’re debating between the Oura Ring and the Samsung Galaxy Ring, we have things to say.

Amazfit is known for its budget-friendly fitness tech that often outperforms what you may expect from an Amazon brand product. The new Helio Ring continues that by offering a smart ring that boasts solid metrics, sleek design, and no subscription fee. It’s especially alluring for users already in the Amazfit ecosystem—this ring pairs seamlessly with devices like the T-Rex 3.

Sources indicate that the Helio Ring includes the basic smart ring metrics: sleep tracking, readiness scoring, heart rate monitoring, and activity logging. It also offers a few innovative features, like built-in AI coaching, which can help you adjust your sleep habits, activity levels, and even recovery tips based on your daily data. The ring is comfortable and well-made, featuring a durable titanium exterior and a fairly slim profile.

That said, if you’re expecting Oura-level insights, you may find the data a little surface-level. It doesn’t really stack up to its competition when it comes to the app and the data. I would say it’s much more of a smart ring for beginners looking to save a few hundred dollars while getting something that is generally useful and looks good on the finger. To go a little deeper, the app is functional, though not especially polished, and some might miss the granularity offered by more premium competitors. Still, for the price—just under $200—the Helio Ring offers a step into smart rings, especially for anyone prioritizing affordability and comfort.

According to recent reports, the first time I put on the Oura Ring 4, I figured that this was as good as it got when it comes to smart rings. Super low profile. Super light. And a charge that lasts for a week. The removal of the nodes in previous generations was the clincher.

Industry observers note that the app and software that come with an Oura Ring come with any of the versions. I am impressed by how small and thin the Oura Ring 5 is. They’ve managed to put that impressive tech into a smaller unit, which is even more discreet. But personally, I find the ring too small, to the point that it feels a little strange and less secure on my finger.

According to recent reports, senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM, still prefers the slim design of the Oura Ring 5, but if you want to score almost all of the same features in a bigger ring, you might want to opt for the Ring 4. You might even score a serious discount, as their last-gen model goes on sale often.

Read More: Our Hands-On Review of the Oura Ring 4.

The Ultrahuman Ring AIR was previously on this list as our Best No-Membership-Needed Smart Ring, but after a legal dispute with another smart ring maker, they could no longer sell that version in the United States.

Sources indicate that we are currently testing a review unit of the Ultrahuman Ring Pro, the brand’s latest offering, which is currently available for pre-order, to see if it’s worth adding to this guide. Ultrahuman is promising a longer battery life, advanced insights, and a more streamlined app experience.

It has been revealed that design is more than just looks—it’s about wearability. Smart rings need to be lightweight enough for 24/7 wear, durable enough for workouts and showers, and comfortable enough that you forget they’re on. Most are made from lightweight metals like titanium or aluminum alloy, and many brands include a sizing kit to find your ideal size. Pay attention to internal sensor placement as well—rings with smooth, node-free interiors are more comfortable for long-term use.

Color and style also matter. While many smart rings come in simple black or silver, several brands offer gold, matte gray, or brushed finishes to suit different tastes (though those options can cost more). Just remember: These rings are not meant to be the flashiest piece of jewelry you wear—they are designed for functionality, and you will notice scratches over time, regardless of the color you choose.

The finger that you place your smart ring on also matters. While a smart ring can still work no matter what finger you place it on, most companies recommend that you place it on your forefinger on your non-dominant hand, because that is where your pulse is the strongest and is less likely to get in the way of daily tasks.

The ring’s hardware is only half the equation—the app experience is where you’ll glean all the information your ring has to offer. Some apps, like Oura and Samsung Health, offer intuitive scoring systems for recovery, readiness, and sleep, plus easy-to-read graphics and insights. Others, like Ultrahuman and Amazfit, may have a steeper learning curve because the interface isn't laid out as intuitively. However, they aren’t outrageously difficult to follow, just a little less categorized than others like Oura and Samsung.

In a recent development, you’ll also want to consider whether the app integrates with your other health platforms, like Apple Health, Google Fit, or Garmin Connect—and whether it provides usable insights, not just raw data. For example, you don’t just want to see a low readiness score—you want to hear from your ring why that score may be too low and how to fix it: "Your activity was through the roof yesterday, maybe take it easy today and find some time to recover." The best apps break down complex biometrics into simple takeaways you can actually use.

According to recent reports, in all our testing with smart rings (and even fitness trackers in general), accuracy has been the hardest metric to measure. For these smart rings, we found that bigger names like Oura and Galaxy Ring had the most consistent results across sleep stages, heart rate, HRV, and temperature tracking. Which makes sense with more funding backing the brand names. We also compared their workout metrics against wrist trackers like the Apple Watch, and accuracy held up for most workouts. Ultrahuman was close behind, especially succeeding in the recovery category. RingConn and Amazfit sometimes highlighted small accuracy inconsistencies, especially with workout differentiation. If you look at the prices here, you’ll see a pattern: The more expensive the ring, the more accurate the data.

Recent findings suggest that these rings aren't meant to give you the most accurate workout training data, though. If you're looking for a device to wear only for your workout, that will provide you with training insights, you are going to want to go for a fitness tracker designed for that situation. If you are going to wear it during your runs or lifts, you may want a wrist or torso tracker. "Nobody really needs to be wearing two fitness trackers at any time," notes Men's Health Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. "Find the one that fits your needs and will give you the best data for your goals.".

Smart rings aren’t medical devices. They offer estimates based on algorithms and sensor data, not lab-verified testing. But if you use them consistently, even numbers that aren’t quite perfect can give you valuable insight into your health patterns over time, as rings will compare your past data against your current data for a more complete picture.

As with most technology, the more you use the product, the more often you have to charge it. Typically, a fully charged smart ring lasts about four to eight days. Oura and RingConn top the list with a full week of use per charge (potentially eight days with light use). Samsung’s Galaxy Ring is also impressive with around seven days. However, less expensive rings generally run closer to four or five days of charge.

Most rings charge via a small dock or case, and a full charge takes about 60 to 90-minutes. Consider how the charging process fits into your routine—especially if you blueprint to wear the ring to sleep. A good time to charge is often in the shower each day (and it's also a good time to clean it). With this method, you’ll never have to leave the ring off for that extended 90 minute charge time. And frankly, you won’t even have to worry about the length of time your ring will hold a charge. I do this with my ring, and I’ve never dipped below a 70% charge (except that one time I forgot my charger on a week-long vacation, oops).

Recent findings suggest that well, that all depends on your individual priorities. Smartwatches generally offer more features: GPS, message notifications, guided workouts, music controls, and in-depth workout analytics. But they also tend to be bulkier, need more frequent charging, and cause screen distractions.

According to recent reports, smart rings, on the other hand, are streamlined, screenless, and usually focused on sleep, stress, recovery, and wellness in general. They’re ideal if you want to track biometrics without getting sucked into a screen every few minutes. For the data-obsessed, wearing a smart ring at night and adding a smartwatch during the day is a great combination.

That mentioned, if you’re a serious runner, cyclist, or athlete who wants workout coaching and performance stats in real time, a smartwatch is likely a better fit. If you’re focused on recovery, sleep quality, and managing stress, a smart ring may be the choice for you.

Its lightweight titanium build and water resistance make it comfortable for 24/7 wear, and the battery reliably lasts up to a week on a single charge. The Oura Ring 4 excels in sleep tracking, heart rate variability monitoring, and daily readiness scoring, with an intuitive app that presents data in a clear, actionable format. For most users, the Ring 4 delivers a seamless, unobtrusive way to monitor overall wellness, making it a favorite among those who dislike wrist-worn trackers.

  • “I tried running, and a few other things, and the weight just crept up,” he told Healthline.
  • Dieting allowed him to lose about 50 pounds, but he would then regain it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for years, Dana Bichler was a competitive weightlifter. He felt fit and strong competing at 200 to 210 pounds. But wear and tear on his body and aging eventually pushed him to step away from weightlifting. Without the training, he began to gain weight slowly and steadily.

“I tried running, and a few other things, and the weight just crept up,” he told Healthline.

Dieting allowed him to lose about 50 pounds, but he would then regain it. At his heaviest, he weighed close to 300 pounds, which inspired him to visit a weight-loss clinic, where he followed a blueprint centered on the clinic’s foods.

Sources indicate that “It’s a life of deprivation,” Bichler said. “You just can’t live like it.”.

About five years ago, he tried a GLP-1 medication and two others a few years later. Each helped him lose weight initially but then stopped working.

“There was really no long-term positive effects or benefits that I saw,” he said.

However, he still takes Mounjaro for blood sugar control because he is prediabetic.

It has been revealed that A few years ago, he was diagnosed with fatty liver disease. His condition was tied to obesity and caused scarring on his liver.

In a recent development, bichler understood the seriousness of the condition as his two younger sisters and his oldest brother also had fatty liver disease. His brother and youngest sister developed cirrhosis, and his brother died after the disease affected other parts of his body.

“I had to do something,” he stated. “What I was doing was not working.”.

Sources indicate that from his home in St. Cloud, Minnesota, Bichler traveled to the University of Minnesota to see a hepatologist, who referred him to a gastroenterologist who had worked with Boston Scientific on the instruments used to perform endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG).

ESG is a minimally invasive weight loss procedure performed using an FDA-authorized endoscopic suturing system, such as one offered through Boston Scientific’s Endura Weight Loss Solutions.

Sources indicate that during ESG, a doctor passes an endoscope through the mouth and uses sutures to fold the stomach into a narrower sleeve. No portion of the stomach is removed, and there are no incisions. The smaller stomach limits how much a person can eat at once.

“Patients typically go home the same day and can return to routine daily activities within two to three days,” Brian Dunkin, MD, chief medical officer at Boston Scientific, told Healthline. “For the right person, that provides another less-invasive option to consider with their healthcare professional.”.

While ESG may be a good option for some people who don’t achieve weight loss goals with GLP-1 medications, can’t tolerate them, or don’t want to stay on medication long term, Dunkin remarked he doesn’t think of it as ESG versus GLP-1 drugs.

“One of the best things GLP-1 medications have done is get more people talking to their doctors about obesity and recognizing it as a chronic disease that deserves treatment,” he said.

Each approach has different benefits, risks, and side effects.

“The goal is finding the right treatment, or combination of treatments, for the right patient at the right time,” said Dunkin.

ESG is indicated for adults with obesity with a BMI between 30 and 50, but Dunkin noted BMI is only part of the conversation. ESG may be an option for people who aren’t getting the weight loss results they want, who don’t want to stay on weight loss medication long term, or for whom bariatric surgery may not be appropriate or desired, he added.

“Obesity is a chronic disease that requires long-term care,” noted Dunkin. “ESG is one part of that care, which is why I believe so strongly in a multidisciplinary approach. The goal is to look at the whole person and find a care blueprint they can sustain over time.”.

In March 2025, Bichler decided ESG was a good fit for him and received the procedure at Boston Scientific. At the time, he was 67 years old and on Medicare, which pre-approved the procedure.

“I just felt comfortable with it not being invasive, and I really needed to deal with [my weight], so I did,” he said.

When Bichler underwent ESG he weighed somewhere in the 260s. Today, he weighs 178 pounds.

While the procedure went smoothly, he noted the following month was difficult. Because bread, pasta, rice, and carbonated drinks were off the table, he had to consume clear liquids, then slowly moved to other liquids, and eventually cream soups.

“I found that extremely difficult,” he remarked.

In a recent development, what surprised him most was depression. Looking back, he calls it a perfect storm. Working with his weight loss doctor, he had stopped taking his antidepressant about two weeks before the procedure. After surgery, his eating habits changed dramatically, disrupting the social life he’d built around food.

“I was in a pretty deep funk for a while,” he said. “I really was.”.

He restarted his antidepressant, and over time, he adjusted to a new way of eating.

Sources indicate that “I’ve discovered I like cream soup,” he noted. “I still have it for meals.”.

According to recent reports, although he’s lost more than 80 pounds, Bichler remarked the bigger change is how good he feels. He exercises four to five days a week and has more energy and moves more easily than he has in years.

According to recent reports, “I haven’t felt this good in 30 years,” Bichler stated. “I’m not kidding you.”.

According to recent reports, he’s able to enjoy things he loves like working on the farm he and his wife own. At the farm, he hunts ducks, turkeys, pheasants, and small game, and runs a trapline, all activities his weight had made nearly impossible for a long time.

“It used to be really hard for me to do because of the physicality of doing some of these things,” he mentioned.

It has been revealed that although he retired from his profession, Bichler remarked he’s busier than ever. He’s a protodeacon in the Eastern Orthodox Church and also serves as a chaplain for his local police department, a role that has him climbing in and out of squad cars and up and down steps.

“Before I’d be sucking air trying to keep up,” he said.

Most meaningful of all is that he has more energy to give to his family.

Sources indicate that “I have a grandson that I can actually do things and be active with now,” Bichler said. “It’s like starting all over. I just feel like a newly introduced person.”.

Electric power tool brand Greenworks is expanding its battery-forward lineup in a huge way with the launch of OPTIMUS, an all-new, go-anywhere electric side-by-side utility vehicle that packs over 100 equivalent hp and a 40 mph top speed.

First shown at Equip Exposition 2026 in Kentucky last month, the newly redesigned Greenworks OPTIMUS UTV is the biggest, baddest, and newest addition to the company’s battery-backed commercial ecosystem. Greenworks claims the latest SxS brings together the brand’s purpose-built equipment and power platforms and is designed to work across the demands of its professional property maintenance customers.

“OPTIMUS has always been about pushing battery power beyond what the industry expects, and the UTV is a natural extension of that vision,” notes Yin Chen, CEO of Greenworks. “We’re bringing professionals more ways to put battery power to work, from the equipment they use to maintain properties to the utility vehicles and charging systems that support their entire operation.”.

Greenworks’ OPTIMUS is built around the company’s 400V high-voltage electrical platform and mates a pair of compact electric motors that combine for 110 equivalent (?) hp. Those motors draw power from a 19 kWh lithium-ion battery pack with enough efficiency to hit a 40 MPH top speed and cover up to 68 miles of range under typical operating conditions.

When it’s time to haul, OPTIMUS offers buyers a 2,500 lb. towing capacity and 1,300 lb. payload capacity along with 11 full inches of ground clearance and a beefy, 6,000 lb. electric winch. Independent suspension, oversized all-terrain tires, torque vectoring differentials, and multiple terrain modes round out the spec sheet and a picture of a machine that’s designed to handle some seriously demanding off-road applications.

Looks expensive but for a gov or organization leasing or buying a latest utv probably price completive with less headache.

The fabric of your moisture-wicking top can either help or hinder sweat management, so you want to make sure you're investing in materials with sweat-wicking technology that can hold up through multiple washes.

#110598. Breaking: Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (798 w)

Breaking: Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (798 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume.
  • According to recent reports, whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation.
  • Industry observers note that to obtain genetic data from whales, marine biologists historically have had to conduct a skin biopsy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume. Whale carcasses will sink to the bottom and become marine life habitats. Whale pee nourishes the entire ocean. But how about whale snot? The microbes and other biological material emitted from their blowholes when the giant cetaceans breathe has helped scientists sequence an entire whale genome: Take that whale vomit. The findings are detailed in a study published today in the journal Molecular Ecology Resources.

According to recent reports, whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation. With genomic data, researchers can measure population health, to see how much genetic diversity and inbreeding is present. It can also help identify individual animals for monitoring, help determine an animal’s sex, and estimate the population’s size.

Industry observers note that to obtain genetic data from whales, marine biologists historically have had to conduct a skin biopsy. They’ll take a dart, stick it into the whale’s blubber, and take a small sample of the skin and blubber. However, during sampling, boats must get close to the whales, which can disturb them. In some locations and for some endangered species, getting close enough to take a biopsy isn’t permitted or possible.

That’s where whale snot—or blow—comes in. For this study, a team from Scotland’s University of St. Andrews, the University of Copenhagen in Denmark, the North Coast Cetacean Society, and Fisheries and Oceans Canada used several small drones off the coast of British Columbia. The drones were equipped with sterile petri dishes to collect the samples.

The team flew the drone through the exhaled breaths of one North pacific humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira) at a time, but still sampled several individual whales. The humpbacks generally took one to six breaths every time they surfaced—covering the drone and the dishes in whale snot.

The team collected 58 blow samples from 26 individual humpback whales. They also took repeated samples from the same whales, collected in different encounters and across two years to match the genomes. They then cross-referenced the genomes collected from the whale blow with genomes sequenced from traditional blubber biopsies taken from the same animals.

To keep the DNA from mixing, the team targeted the whale most upwind in the pod, since the blow downwind might mix with the blow from the whales up ahead. Resting whales were never sampled, and the team stopped the drone flights if a whale showed any reaction. More than one third of samples were collected by flying the drone directly from land—no boat required.

The DNA was sequenced to produce two types of genomes. Low-coverage nuclear genomes, which are inherited from both parents, and high-coverage mitochondrial genomes, which are inherited from the mother only.

Sources indicate that the team found that the genetic diversity estimated from the blow samples was very similar to the estimates taken from traditional biopsies. Fortunately, the humpback population in the study demonstrates little evidence of recent inbreeding. There is a small proportion of the genome that has long stretches of identical DNA, but the team believes that most likely reflects distant shared ancestry or past population bottlenecks.

According to recent reports, according to the team, this research marks one of the first whole genome datasets for a group of North Pacific humpback whales. Previously, only one North Pacific humpback whole genome was publicly available.

It has been revealed that “We will use these blow-derived genomes to not only assess population structure and health, but also assess kinship and family ties among humpback whales foraging in northern British Columbia,” Dr. Éadin O’Mahony, a study co-author and marine mammal ecologist who was at the University of St. Andrews at the time of the study, stated in a statement. “The aim is to understand how their social bonds form: Are the whales that forage together family, or long-term friends?”.

As expected, the North Pacific humpback whales were genetically distinct from their counterparts living in the North Atlantic. This confirms that data taken from whale blow works as well from data taken from conventional biopsies. The drone-captured genetic analyses also correctly determined every whale’s sex, and revealed three previously undescribed mitochondrial DNA variants, which could help show how some of these whales are related. The blow from whales swimming in groups also did not have any sign of contamination from neighboring whales.

About 16 percent of the DNA in each blow sample were also primarily from the microbes living in the whale’s airways. According to the team, this indicates that a single breath could tell us about the individual whale and its respiratory microbiome, opening up a potential new window into cetacean health.

That’s a whole lot of data from just a little bit of snot.

#110593. Hormone Therapy May Boost Weight Loss on Wegovy, But Not as Much on Zepbound

📅 26 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (912 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

Hormone Therapy May Boost Weight Loss on Wegovy, But Not as Much on Zepbound

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Females using menopause hormone therapy (MHT) alongside GLP-1 medications such as Ozempic or Wegovy may experience greater weight loss, according to a study presented at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the Menopause Society.
  • Weight gain is a common concern among middle-aged women.
  • GLP-1 medications have been shown to be effective for weight loss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Females using menopause hormone therapy (MHT) alongside GLP-1 medications such as Ozempic or Wegovy may experience greater weight loss, according to a study presented at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the Menopause Society.

Weight gain is a common concern among middle-aged women. While much of this is associated with aging, hormonal changes during menopause can also contribute to changes in body fat and its distribution.

GLP-1 medications have been shown to be effective for weight loss. However, the results may vary by sex and reproductive stage.

For example, studies have found that women and adults under age 55 may experience greater weight loss with these medications.

A previous small observational study in postmenopausal women found that using MHT alongside semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, was associated with greater weight loss.

However, whether hormone therapy influences weight loss outcomes with different GLP-1 medications remains unclear.

To investigate this question, researchers compared weight loss in middle-aged women receiving either semaglutide or tirzepatide, with or without MHT. The findings have not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal.

The study included 3,855 women with an average age of 57 and an average body mass index (BMI) of 36 kg/m2.

The semaglutide cohort included 2,379 individuals, while the tirzepatide cohort included 1,476 individuals.

In a recent development, the average follow-up in the semaglutide cohort, both with and without MHT, was 26 months. The average follow-up in the tirzepatide group was 17 months for those using MHT and 16 months for those not using it.

The researchers found that in the semaglutide cohort, those using MHT alongside the GLP-1 medication had significantly greater weight loss at 9 months than those not using MHT.

Recent findings suggest that these differences were sustained at 12 and 15 months and at the final follow-up. Those using MHT were also more likely to reach up to a 30% total body weight loss than those not using it.

Industry observers note that in the tirzepatide cohort, those using MHT had a modestly greater weight loss at 3 months and were more likely to achieve more than 5% total body weight loss by the final follow-up. However, no significant difference in weight loss was observed at later time points.

According to recent reports, these findings suggest that MHT use may be associated with greater weight loss among middle-aged women taking semaglutide. However, the researchers did not observe a sustained, statistically significant difference in weight loss among those taking tirzepatide.

Betul Hatipoglu, MD, Director of the Diabetes and Obesity Center at the University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, who was not involved in the study, told Healthline that the findings are encouraging.

However, she also cautioned that people should be careful not to interpret them as evidence that hormone therapy should be added to GLP-1 treatment specifically to enhance weight loss.

“This is an association, and the study provides an opportunity to discuss how menopause, aging, changes in body composition, and metabolic health can be present,” she said.

Industry observers note that it is notable to keep in mind that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved certain hormone therapy medications to treat menopause symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. However, these medications are not FDA-approved for weight loss or obesity management.

The study authors noted that larger studies are needed to confirm their observations and to inform individualized strategies for middle-aged females.

In a recent development, sherry Ross, MD, board certified OB-GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who was not involved in the study, noted that weight gain is one of the most common concerns she hears from women during menopause. Beyond affecting self-esteem and quality of life, excess abdominal fat can increase the risk of type 2 diabetes and heart disease.

“Finding effective, sustainable ways to manage weight is important for women’s long-term health and healthy aging,” she stated.

“I would like to see prospective, randomized studies examining GLP-1 medications with and without hormone therapy to determine whether hormone therapy directly improves weight loss and helps women maintain it over time. In the meantime, treatment decisions should be individualized and guided by a healthcare professional.”.

Ross advised that the decision should be based on your individual symptoms, health history, and treatment goals.

Sources indicate that “Hormone therapy can significantly improve disruptive menopausal symptoms, including hot flashes, sleep disturbances, and mood changes. By helping women feel better and more energetic, it may also make it easier to exercise and manage their weight,” she said.

Hatipoglu noted that GLP-1-based medications, on the other hand, are effective treatments for obesity and can improve notable aspects of metabolic health. Their use should be based on an individual’s weight-related health risks, medical history, and treatment goals.

Recent findings suggest that “For a woman who has both bothersome menopausal symptoms and obesity, it may be entirely appropriate to consider both treatments. But I would not recommend starting hormone therapy solely to improve the weight-loss response to a GLP-1 medication based on the evidence right now available,” she mentioned.

Industry observers note that “It is also notable to remember that successful weight management during and after menopause is about more than the number on the scale. Preserving muscle mass, maintaining bone health, improving metabolic health, and supporting long-term physical function are equally important.”.

You should speak with your healthcare professional about the risks and benefits of all treatment options.

Elderly Florida man leads police on wild 16 mph e-bike chase. Thank goodness they caught him

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Residents of Fresh Smyrna Beach, Florida, can finally breathe a sigh of relief.
  • According to the Volusia Sheriff’s Office, 75-year-old Robert Joseph Mitchell was riding his electric bicycle along the beach on November 13 when a sheriff’s deputy clocked him traveling 16 mph in a 10 mph zone (26 km/h in a 16 km/h zone).
  • The deputy attempted to stop Mitchell, who allegedly responded with a middle finger and some choice words before continuing on his way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Residents of Fresh Smyrna Beach, Florida, can finally breathe a sigh of relief. A dangerous menace to society has been taken off the streets after police apprehended a 75-year-old man accused of leading deputies on a high-stakes electric bike chase at speeds reaching a blistering 16 mph (26 km/h).

According to the Volusia Sheriff’s Office, 75-year-old Robert Joseph Mitchell was riding his electric bicycle along the beach on November 13 when a sheriff’s deputy clocked him traveling 16 mph in a 10 mph zone (26 km/h in a 16 km/h zone).

The deputy attempted to stop Mitchell, who allegedly responded with a middle finger and some choice words before continuing on his way.

What followed was apparently the world’s slowest police chase.

Mitchell reportedly continued riding along the beach, eventually exiting onto city streets, where he allegedly rode against traffic before making it back to his home. Deputies followed him, and when Mitchell attempted to retreat into his garage, he reportedly resisted arrest by grabbing onto a golf cart and refusing to let go.

In a recent development, the ordeal ended with Mitchell in custody, facing four charges, including felony fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement, resisting an officer without violence, speeding on the beach, and riding outside the designated beach driving area. His bond was set at $4,000.

And just like that, another dangerous electric bicycle criminal was brought to justice. This was clearly a success story like no other, and American streets are now safer.

Now, before anyone gets too worked up, let’s be clear: I’m not suggesting that e-bike riders should be allowed to ignore traffic laws, endanger pedestrians, or flee from police. Reports indicate that Mitchell was riding recklessly around beachgoers, including children, and that’s certainly something worth addressing. And once he allegedly decided to flee from deputies, he turned what could have been a minor infraction into a much more serious situation.

But can we also acknowledge how absurd this whole thing is?

We’ve reached a point where a 75-year-old man riding a bicycle at 16 mph can end up the subject of a police pursuit and felony charges, while we’ve largely accepted that multi-ton vehicles routinely kill and seriously injure people on our roads as an unavoidable cost of modern transportation.

Sources indicate that every day, drivers speed through neighborhoods, roll through stop signs, stare at their phones, and operate vehicles capable of killing pedestrians with a moment’s inattention. Or perhaps I shouldn’t say ‘capable’, but rather that they do. 40,000 people every year die in the US from car violence. Yet somehow, electric bicycles have become one of the great transportation menaces of our time, despite contributing much, much less to major bodily harm or death.

And yes, there are absolutely legitimate concerns about dangerous riding. I’ve repeatedly argued that we need better enforcement, especially when it comes to teenagers riding high-powered electric dirt bikes and e-motos at 40 mph (64 km/h) down sidewalks and bike paths. Those aren’t electric bicycles, and treating them as such has created a real problem for everyone.

But if we’re going to devote police resources to cracking down on dangerous two-wheeled behavior, perhaps we could start there instead of turning a 1 mph beach ride into the crime of the century.

According to recent reports, what is absurd is that he didn't simply stop and follow the officer's directions to slow down. If he is going to try to flee from the police by riding dangerously including going against traffic then he should face charges. As presumably a first time offender, he'll be given probation if he agrees not to do it again.

Industry observers note that to be fair, Mitchell’s alleged behavior after being stopped certainly didn’t help his case. But the larger point remains: our priorities around road safety have become wildly distorted.

We’ve normalized the dangers of cars so thoroughly that we barely blink at the daily carnage they cause, yet we’re increasingly treating comparatively low-speed electric bicycles as an existential threat to public safety.

I’m all for enforcing sensible e-bike rules. I’m all for throwing the book at major infractions and scofflaws who pose a public menace. But I’m also for applying a little perspective.

It has been revealed that because if a 75-year-old man riding an electric bicycle at 16 mph is among our most pressing transportation safety concerns, then I have some very good news about the state of our roads. But unfortunately, there is no good news to share today.

#110591. Coffee could have anti-aging benefits. Here’s why.

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1140 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Coffee could have anti-aging benefits. Here’s why.

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1140 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are a handful of foods and beverages—red wine, eggs, and cooking oils—whose reputations tend to pendulum-swing routinely between “lifesaving” and “death sentence.” I usually hedge my bets by eating these confusing foods in moderation.
  • The one item I have trouble consuming in moderation might be the most contentious of all: coffee.
  • In a recent development, despite my unwavering devotion to coffee, the jury is still out on whether my daily fix is actually good for my health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are a handful of foods and beverages—red wine, eggs, and cooking oils—whose reputations tend to pendulum-swing routinely between “lifesaving” and “death sentence.” I usually hedge my bets by eating these confusing foods in moderation.

The one item I have trouble consuming in moderation might be the most contentious of all: coffee. I am so hopelessly addicted to the stuff that I usually need at least one cup of coffee before going out to meet a friend for coffee.

In a recent development, despite my unwavering devotion to coffee, the jury is still out on whether my daily fix is actually good for my health. Throughout my lifetime, coffee has variously been purported to protect my heart, disrupt its rhythm, reduce my risk of cancer, and increase it. All I know is it helps me become a fully conscious person every morning. But could my coffee habit actually reduce wrinkles and help me age more gracefully?

A new study conducted at Texas A&M suggests that certain compounds in coffee might protect the body against aging and inflammation.

Sources indicate that however, according to Dr. Dung Trinh, the chief medical officer at Healthy Brain Clinic in Long Beach, California, it’s probably too soon to pop open the champagne (or brew a celebratory pot) over the potential perks of your coffee habit.

“It’s far too early to treat coffee—or caffeic acid—as an anti-aging intervention,” Trinh tells Popular Science.

Despite its inconsistent status as a health food, coffee has been consistently linked to longer life and a lower likelihood of certain diseases, though it’s not certain why. The Texas A&M study, led by Dr. Stephen Safe, focused on a cellular receptor called NR4A1.

Sources indicate that NR4A1 is a protein that regulates how cells respond to stress and damage. The study found that several compounds in coffee, particularly polyphenols—plant compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties—bind to the NR4A1 receptor. One of these polyphenols, caffeic acid, is found in coffee and many other plants and, despite its name, has nothing to do with caffeine. These compounds seem to promote NR4A1’s protective effects, including mitigating cellular damage and slowing the growth of cancer cell line in laboratory models.

Industry observers note that in other words, the harder your NR4A1 proteins are working, the better your cells may be at fending off damage. Sign me up!

Recent findings suggest that after researchers removed NR4A1 from cells in the lab, those benefits stopped, suggesting this receptor may help produce them. So, if coffee really helps NR4A1 do its job, we might just have a newly introduced anti-aging drink on our hands.

Sources indicate that interestingly, caffeine does not appear to play a key part in this mechanism, Trinh claims. Instead, those benefits seem to come from coffee’s other compounds, like caffeic acid and its fellow polyphenols.

Sources indicate that “What stood out to me was that the story was not really about caffeine,” he claims. “I also found it interesting that the researchers did more than simply show that these compounds could bind to the receptor—they demonstrated NR4A1-dependent effects in cells. That makes the mechanism more compelling.”.

Translation: The study didn’t just show that coffee compounds attach to NR4A1; it showed that this binding actually seems to activate the protein’s protective effects.

Consistent with this, the study also found that decaf coffee demonstrated similar protective effects on the lab cells, providing further evidence that coffee’s benefits may not have anything to do with caffeine at all.

Recent findings suggest that “One of the interesting messages from this paper is that coffee should not be thought of as simply a delivery system for caffeine,” Trinh states. “Caffeic acid, chlorogenic acid, ferulic acid, and several other coffee compounds all interacted with NR4A1, while caffeine revealed much more variable NR4A1-related activity.”.

So, coffee’s superpower might not come from caffeine at all, at least when it comes to anti-aging benefits.

Before you start guzzling triple lattes in the name of cellular protection, know that “more” does not always mean “better.”.

“We simply cannot infer from this study that more coffee means more NR4A1 benefit,” Trinh notes. This is because the researchers studied coffee extracts and purified compounds in a lab setting rather than giving human subjects increasing amounts of coffee and measuring NR4A1 activity. Plus, in human biology, it’s possible to have too much of a good thing, Trinh says.

It has been revealed that “At some point, additional coffee can bring unwanted effects from caffeine, including sleep disruption, anxiety, palpitations, or increases in blood pressure in susceptible people,” he notes. “Those effects could counteract other health benefits. So, this study should not be interpreted as establishing either an optimal number of cups or a dose-response relationship for this pathway.”.

Trinh adds that as compelling as the study’s findings are, he doesn’t yet believe they justify changing recommendations around coffee consumption.

Recent findings suggest that earlier studies have linked coffee drinking to living longer and to better outcomes for some age-related conditions, Trinh notes. But those studies couldn’t explain why. This one offers “one possible biological explanation,” he says.

Like most early-stage research, Trinh says, this study can’t be applied to humans sipping their morning “cup of ambition.” Much of the work used a specific cancer cell in the lab, along with mouse immune cells, rather than testing regular human coffee drinkers directly. And while the study identified a potentially promising mechanism, it’s not clear how this mechanism will translate to human health outcomes.

Ultimately, Trinh notes, no single food or compound is likely to be the deciding factor in how well we age.

For a coffee addict like myself, though, these findings are the best kind of wake-up call. Coffee may or may not turn back the clock, but it does stop me from hitting snooze 15 times.

“The much bigger determinants of healthy aging remain things such as regular physical activity, good sleep, avoiding smoking, controlling blood pressure and metabolic risk, maintaining social and cognitive engagement, and eating an overall nutritious diet,” Trinh says.

“This study is a promising piece of the scientific puzzle, not a prescription for another cup of coffee.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, SLING BAGS ARE here to stay, gentlemen, and to be honest, they’re a lighter and smarter way to commute with your EDC when backpacks and duffel bags feel like overkill. Worn across the body (unlike a fanny pack, which is designed to sit around the waist), sling bags are easy to carry, super practical, and able to transport all your daily essentials using a bunch of accessible compartments, zippers, and pockets. The best sling bags for men offer a range of styles for every kind of guy, whether you’re commuting, traveling, or heading into the outdoors. Some are minimal and sleek, while others favor the rugged and technical.

If you’re stuck on which sling bag to pick, don’t sweat it—our team tested and narrowed down the top contenders. Below, we’ve included 11 standout picks that combine comfort, style, and hands-free functionality from notable brands like Peak Design, Lululemon, and The North Face.

According to recent reports, we gave 20 different sling bags a test run, but Lululemon’s offering takes the cake. The Everywhere Belt Bag is all about making things easier for the man on the go. For starters, you can throw it over your shoulder or wear it around your waist like a fanny pack for when you're on the trail or at an outdoor concert (or any other time you want to be hands-free). The main pouch features a double two-way zipper that opens three-quarters of the way, letting you see and reach everything inside without having to dig around blindly. Another bonus: There’s a smaller pocket tucked into the back with a single zipper, which makes it ideal for hiding cash, cards, and other small valuables.

Recent findings suggest that thanks to the water-resistant nylon exterior, anything stowed away will remain dry, in the event it starts pouring rain. Our favorite part, however, is the strap that we found to be one of the most comfortable ones that we’ve tested. As for the colorway, you can choose from a bunch of neutral tones, but our fashion team recommends going with the eucalyptus hue—you’re bound to be the center of attention.

While it can’t store a water bottle, we love how effortlessly our gadgets and snacks fit inside. Not to mention, it has so much versatility in regard to style. You can wear it with your best sweatsuit or casual fit and look fly for the day’s festivities.

Read More: Best Fanny Packs for Men.

This Amazon best-seller is spot-on for your next adventure. It’s really got organization in spades with mesh pockets on two sides for bottles or umbrellas, a small front zipper pocket for smaller devices, and a significant space inside that’s designed like a backpack. It’s smartly compartmentalized into smaller sections for anything from keys, passports, snacks, and other bits and bobs. During a camping trip, we made use of the main pocket inside, which is big enough to store your phone and tablet, a feature that we deemed essential in a travel sling bag.

You can even enjoy your music on your commute as the convenient opening on the front provides easy access to your earphones. It comes in every color imaginable, but the teal blue and reflective details will help you stand out and offer nighttime visibility. And unlike others in this guide, this one comes with a water bottle holder, so you stay hydrated on the move.

Read More: Best Backpacks for Men.

As one of the smaller sling bags in our guide, the Topo Designs Mini Quick Pack has substantial storage where it matters most. We found that its capacity is perfect for shorter trips and daily errands, and the straps are a piece of cake to adjust (though there are quite a few straps). Whenever we don’t need a huge backpack and want to pack light, this little guy is a star.

Sources indicate that in our experience, we’ve worn it on the waist and across the body. One tester was able to utilize the bike light attachment loop for a nighttime ride to increase visibility. And with a solid amount of space and interior organization for a phone, cardholder, and other odds and ends, our editors have also tucked it under a thin coat when we’re in a tight spot. Plus, the unique color-blocked design earns it some extra style points.

In a recent development, while we still feel it works great for the city, this ruggedly built sling is perfect for outdoor adventurists. Firstly, it’s offered in two different sizes with a 6- or 9-liter size, ensuring that if you need a little extra space, you can spend an extra $10 to upgrade. Even in the smaller size, you can easily fit a water bottle plus all of your other gear like earbuds, sunglasses, phone, EDC essentials, protein bar, plus more thanks to the expandable gusset.

Recent findings suggest that one of the cool features of this bag that you won’t find on others is that it comes with sturdy quick-release buckles on both sides, making it ideal no matter which shoulder you toss it around. It offers various storage compartments, 10 to be exact, even with a soft-lined pouch that is great for your phone or sunglasses, helping to avoid scratching while on the move—plus, the padded back and bottom help to protect everything else. Its water resistance and six-year warranty make it the perfect outdoor bag.

Sources indicate that the North Face’s Base Camp Voyager Sling is basically a mini backpack in disguise that’s built to take a beating. This thing held up through packed subways, bike rides, and overhead bin shoves without a single scuff. The shell’s made from abrasion-resistant polyester fabric, the same ultra-tough material as the brand’s duffels, which are designed for actual expeditions, so your daily commute? No sweat.

There’s a padded sleeve that snugly fits a tablet, reflective accents for low-light visibility (great for late-night rides), and a thick, padded shoulder strap that’s actually comfortable to wear all day. Bonus: There’s a zip pocket on the strap that perfectly fits your phone, so no more digging around at crosswalks.

Industry observers note that we also loved how the design leans more toward a backpack than a bag. It’s minimalist, structured, and doesn’t flop around when you’re on the move. Whether you’re weaving through downtown foot traffic or navigating an airport terminal, this is the kind of sling that keeps up, and doesn’t look out of place when you stop for a coffee.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for a more elevated sling, then you’ll definitely want to grab this leather Blake Belt Bag from Leatherology. We recommend opting for the standard-size model, as it holds about 5 liters, but it also comes in slim and mini models. You can choose from 10 colors, including three in smooth full-grain, six in pebbled full-grain, a black croc leather, and a groovy fairway green color (very reminiscent of The Masters’ signature color).

Recent findings suggest that the adjustable strap is quite versatile, with the options of wearing it as a traditional crossbody bag, hanging off one shoulder, or around the waist, though, as it’s a unisex model, the strap may be just a touch too short for some guys. That remarked, it can hold a good amount of gear with its main zippered compartment, which comes with four interior card slots and a decent-sized interior mesh pocket that is also zippered. While some note that the zippers are a little stiff, over time they do tend to wear in and work much easier. Plus, for an additional fee, you can personalize it to truly make it one of a kind.

Eddie Bauer’s Mini Crossbody Bag proves that you don’t have to spend big to get a reliable everyday carry. Made from nylon, this compact bag punches above its weight when it comes to utility. During testing, we found the slightly 0.8L capacity to be just right. It’s big enough to fit your phone, wallet, keys, and a lip balm, but small enough to stay light and nimble when you’re clocking your daily step count goal. I love the front cargo pocket that has a flap closure. It kept essentials like subway cards or AirPods secure but easy to access when we were on the go.

Yeah, it’s too small to carry a tablet or water bottle, but it comes in clutch for light carry days and quick errands. One tester wore it on a weekend trip and appreciated how easy it was to sling over a jacket without ever feeling bulky. The strap adjusts smoothly and stays comfortable during hours of walking, and after a few days of use, the bag still looked good as new.

Reigning Champ’s crossbody bag is reliable for outdoor gear because it combines smart construction and water-resistant materials. This resilient twill bag is the practical choice to go anywhere, and though it may look compact, there’s plenty of space and interior pockets to keep your stuff organized without looking overloaded. I even wore this during a rainy evening commute, and everything inside, from my phone to loose bills, stayed bone dry.

It has been revealed that the adjustable webbing strap is quite comfortable, even if you strategy on wearing it all day long. With it, you get two main zippered pockets, plus an internal zippered pocket, and you even get a small front-facing zippered pocket for quick access when you need it. Though it only comes in one color, there’s really not a more versatile accessory color than black, anyway. And it looks darn good with a slight pop of white in its logo.

Recent findings suggest that we love a bag that comes in more than one size, and the Everyday Sling from Peak Design comes in three different sizes: 3-, 6-, and 10-liter options, making it one of the most versatile choices available. Not only that, but it’s also available in seven different colors, ensuring that whatever your taste is, there is definitely a pick for you. Another thing that we really like about this bag is the ability to loosen (or tighten) the quick-adjuster and padded straps while still wearing it.

While this bag is designed with creatives in mind to be able to hold all of your tech, like cameras, laptops (depending on size choice), lenses, rangefinders, and more (thanks to its comfy and padded design), it can still be a great option to use hiking or biking with its weatherproof design and 400D shell construction. While it is resistant to the elements, some reviewers do mention to be cautious with heavier rainfall, though the majority note it can handle most situations.

Traveling around the city, either to and from work, running errands, or just heading to the local coffee shop means finding a bag that’s just big enough to hold the essentials, yet one that’s not gonna weigh you down. Aer’s City Sling 2 is the perfectly sized bag for city activities and commuting. It weighs under a pound and holds 2.5 liters, which means you can still get all of your EDC gear in there with ease.

Even though it’s lightweight, it’s darn tough with its 700D Cordura nylon design and aircraft-grade aluminum tension locks, which means you don’t sacrifice durability. It has a quick-access front pocket for things like keychains, while its back zippered pocket is better for valuables like passports or wallets, with ample room in its main zippered compartment, too. Plus, its strap hides away thanks to its magnetic fastener, converting it into a mobile dopp kit in a pinch. While the strap is tough, it may be a little rough on the shoulder after a day of wear.

Oakley’s Extractor Sling is basically a backpack in disguise, making it perfect for work commutes. It has the capacity to serve as one with several compartments and pockets to transport goods like your hand cream, portable charger, and office laptop. We found this sling bag specifically useful for when we want to pack more without overdoing it.

You can even fit your gym shorts and workout shirts inside to hit a quick session once you’re off the clock. Plus, the back panel is equipped with air channels to help deliver more breathability and comfort while you’re on the move. Although the downside is that it is heavier than others we’ve tested, it’s got the volume you need to load it all in.

The best sling bags for men should offer features that cater to your needs. Typically smaller than a messenger bag, they can be worn across the body, over a shoulder, or even around the waist. The sling bags in our guide range from 1.5 liters of capacity to 30 liters.

It has been revealed that when looking for one, consider the layout and accessibility of the compartments, pockets, and dedicated spaces for laptops, smartphones, tablets, or water bottles. All in all, there should be ample storage capacity (usually measured and listed in liters) that allows for smart organization and easy reach.

Since sling bags are often worn over one shoulder or across the body, the best sling bags for men need to have adjustable straps and padding to distribute weight evenly across your shoulders and back—a properly fitted sling bag should feel comfortable and not strain you even when worn for extended periods. Therefore, pay attention to the strap’s material, width, and adjustability.

Sources indicate that A lightweight sling bag is usually better since it is easier to carry and feels better on your body by preventing unnecessary strain on your shoulders and back, especially if you blueprint to use the sling bag for hours on end, or carry it while hiking. Ultimately, the weight of a sling bag will depend on the bag's capacity, design, and intended uses.

Sources indicate that to find the best sling bags for men, myself and Joseph Cheatham, led by our Senior Gear and Reviews Editor Ryan Brower, put them through real-life situations. We loaded them up with our usual gear like our phone, wallet, keys, snacks, even a water bottle to see how they handle the weight. The ones we tested have been worn at outdoor festivals, during day hikes, through long-haul flights, and of course, out and about running weekend errands. We paid close attention to the pockets and zippers, but really made sure to assess how comfortable the adjustable straps lie on our shoulders.

Sources indicate that many sling bags are actually designed to accommodate laptops or tablets. These sling bags usually fall on the larger, more functional side, with a large capacity and spacious interior compartment, as well as dedicated padded compartments or sleeves that offer protection and secure storage for your electronic devices.

Sling bags are versatile just like backpacks, hence, with the right style and design, they can work in a variety of places. A sleek, leather option looks professional enough for the office and goes well with your office fits. A rugged, weather-resistant one is great for outdoor activities—in fact, there are sling bags designed for purposes like hiking and traveling. For your casual outings, a small, stylish sling bag will work wonders.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you wake up tomorrow as the esteemed Lord Mayor of London, you’ll want to make a properly dignified entrance. To make sure your arrival turns the right heads, Electrogenic has taken the Mayor’s 1973 Roll-Royce Phantom VI and turned it into a properly traditional standard-bearer with modern electric power.

The stately, stylish, and silent electric Rolls-Royce car made its public debut at last month’s Salon Privé weekend at Blenheim Palace, where it joined a growing fleet of classic Rollers that have received Elctrogenic’s electric conversion, including the stunning Mulliner-bodied 1929 Phantom II that we covered back in 2023.

According to recent reports, for this project, Electrogenic carefully removed the internal combustion-based engine, transmission, and fuel system from the City of London Corporation’s official ’73 Phantom VI limo and replaced it with a 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motor putting out 310 Nm (~230 lb-ft) of torque. Sharp-eyed readers will note those numbers are significantly lower than what you’d expect from the 6.2L L410 V8 fitted with twin SU carburetors (as it was in the standard ’73 IV), but since those numbers were never officially published, we would say that the power available from the new electric drivetrain is similarly adequate for Mayoral use.

Power for the electric motor comes from a 62 kWh li-ion battery fitted under the hood bonnet, and offers more than enough range to get the Lord Mayor to their appointments in and around the city.

To ensure the heads of the heads of the city don’t bob in an undignified manner while on parade, Electrogenic added a “ceremonial” drive mode that trims power and torque and softens the throttle map, so the chauffeur can more easily hold the crawling pace demanded by civic processions and state occasions.

It has been revealed that “We were honored to be asked to electrify this significant motor car, and to play a part in the City of London Corporation’s journey to net zero,” says Steve Drummond, chief executive of Electrogenic. “When it was debuted in the late 1960s, the Rolls-Royce VI was the most refined and dignified limousine on the road. Now, thanks to electrification, its core character has been enhanced further: it is whisper quiet, effortless to drive with swift performance, and emits zero tailpipe emissions.”.

It's vital for government to be seen to follow it's own policy.

A standard complaint by oil lobbyists is that government vehicles aren't electrified.

Recent findings suggest that only 374 Phantom VIs were built between 1968 and 1990, with this 3 meter-long coach-built limousine having been commissioned during the mayoralty of Alderwoman Dame Susan Langley DBE, the 697th Lord Mayor of the City of London. The Phantom was converted as part of the Corporation’s broader effort to achieve a net zero carbon emissions goal from its own operations in 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even Alaska’s bears are not immune from accidentally making things weird or getting a bit too close.
  • Industry observers note that “Sometimes the bears at Anan share the creek… a little too closely,” the rangers write.
  • For this bit of humor, the rangers awarded the unnamed bears with the 2026 You Made it Weird Award.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even Alaska’s bears are not immune from accidentally making things weird or getting a bit too close. Over the summer, rangers at Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska watched an odd interaction between two unnamed black bears (Ursus americanus) taking part in Anan Creek’s salmon run.

Industry observers note that “Sometimes the bears at Anan share the creek… a little too closely,” the rangers write. “One bear is waiting his turn for a prime fishing spot, and the other is so focused on the fish he doesn’t mind his surroundings. Did the 1st bear make it weird by backing up, or did the 2nd bear make it weird by staying there?”.

For this bit of humor, the rangers awarded the unnamed bears with the 2026 You Made it Weird Award.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

The largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in the region. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their antics.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you're short on space (or even if you're not), having an extra set of drawers on hand is a huge boon for small bedrooms. That's where the best storage beds come in. I'm all about bedroom furniture that does more for your sleep setup, so I gathered up a few favorites from the AD staff. These storage bed picks include sleek, streamlined designs with completely concealed side storage, queen- and king-size beds with pullouts at the footboard, and more. Each one stows generously while you sleep.

A storage bed frame need not be ugly, even if function is the whole point of buying one. In fact, I tapped other editors and we found impressive wooden beds from Thuma and West Elm, the upholstered storage beds of our minimalist dreams from Saatva, Article, and Sundays, and a lilac velvet showpiece from CB2 for anyone who wants their storage bed to be the loudest thing in the room. The market has our back on this one, especially for those of us living in shoebox bedrooms where a queen bed barely fits, let alone a nightstand (the luxury). Below are the 10 storage beds I considered up to snuff, with editor commentary.

All prices in this article reflect queen-size beds unless otherwise noted.

All prices in this article reflect queen-size beds unless otherwise noted.

Industry observers note that delivery and Assembly: The last thing you want is to wait months for your bed frame to help you organize (and elevate) your space. We selected options that offer reasonable shipping windows (usually within one month from placing your order to its arrival at your home) as well as white glove delivery to help set up the storage bed in your desired room, or a frame simple enough to assemble yourself.

Sources indicate that design: A major passion of ours at AD is finding furniture that is not only functional but is also not an eyesore. We skipped clunky bed frames and included pieces that can sit comfortably anywhere in modern and minimalist bedrooms and beyond.

Size: Our editors tested a mix of queen and king sizes, and prices in this story reflect queens. We looked for picks that come in a range of sizes to accommodate any space. Keep in mind that storage beds often have features like pull-out drawers and lift-up bases, so be sure to measure your space and compare it to your desired storage bed's dimensions to ensure the bed can open properly in your bedroom.

It has been revealed that storage Features: The storage bed you select should align with your space. If you're tight on floor space, consider a storage bed that lifts up. If you have low ceilings, consider a storage bed that has drawers underneath.

Durability: We tested storage beds by sleeping on them night after night, taking notice of any factors like creakiness or wobbliness. We also looked for options with high-quality materials like fine upholstery and solid wood that are designed to last.

It has been revealed that price: Storage beds run from a few hundred dollars to well over $2,000, and our picks span that whole range. While the price isn't always the biggest indicator of quality, materials like bouclé and solid wood are usually found in more high-end storage beds.

What Are the Different Types of Storage Beds?

Lift-up beds: Also called an "ottoman bed," this is a model where the mattress base lifts up with the aid of gas struts (pressurized cylinders that do most of the lifting for you), which retailers often call hydraulic lifts. This typically offers the most room out of the storage bed options.

Drawer beds: Fairly self-explanatory: drawers (either under, alongside, or at the foot of the bed) are this frame’s storage approach.

Headboard storage beds: A headboard storage bed draws from mid-century styles, where built-in shelves or nightstands create storage opportunities. This is a good option if what you need to store is also aesthetically pleasing.

Cubby beds: Instead of drawers, these cubbies are open shelving solutions underneath the bed frame, particularly suitable for holding books if you’re looking for a stylish way to create a bedroom library.

What’s a “Hydraulic Lift” in a Storage Bed?

According to recent reports, when your storage bed has interior storage (in other words, when you lift the mattress base upward to access its storage), it needs a lift mechanism to make it possible for you to lift the bed without breaking your back, and to keep the slatted frame upright while you lift your items in and out. Most use gas struts, though you'll often see them sold as hydraulic. If your storage bed has interior storage and no lift, you will collapse yourself and ultimately be pancaked by your own sleep-and-store investment.

What Features Should I Look for in the Best Storage Beds?

A good storage bed, in our opinion, doesn't look like a storage bed. It looks like a regular bed. It's crafted from, ideally, kiln-dried hardwood, it has a slatted base so you don't need to bother with a box spring, and it has non-sticky drawers (thank you, Thuma) or a lift mechanism to help with the lifting of interior storage (thank you, Saatva). Look for a solid wood base, linen upholstery, and invest in some vacuum-sealed bags. I live by these.

What Materials Make a Good Storage Bed?

Recent findings suggest that you're primarily searching for durability and space in storage bed models. Look for frames made from solid wood since this type of material is typically sturdy and long-lasting. A lift mechanism makes storage more accessible without back-breaking exercises. While upholstered beds are a popular favorite, make sure what lies beneath the textile is also going to stand the test of time.

#110582. This Is How Fast You Should Walk to Help Lower Your Risk of Death

📅 26 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1282 w)
